buzzRounds.topic: Dylan Larkin traded from Detroit to Montreal
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Detroit Red Wings traded center Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens on Sunday for prospect Michael Hage, Kirby Dach, goalie Samuel Montembeault and draft picks, including two first-round picks. Larkin had asked for a trade in June. He made his Canadiens debut on Monday, November 23, and set up Alex Newhook's goal, but Montreal lost 2-1 to the Los Angeles Kings.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Larkin is coming off his fifth straight 30-goal season, and the deal moves a big-name center between two Atlantic Division rivals.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Detroit traded Dylan Larkin to Montreal on Sunday, and in his first game as a Canadien on Monday he had an assist in a 2-1 loss to the Kings.

details.name: Dylan Larkin
details.buzz: Larkin assisted on Alex Newhook's second-period goal in his Montreal debut, a day after the trade from Detroit that sent two first-round picks the other way.

buzzRounds.topic: Maple Leafs snap a nine-game losing streak
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Toronto Maple Leafs beat the New York Islanders 4-2 on Monday, November 23, ending a nine-game losing streak (0-8-1) that dated back to Halloween. Eighteen-year-old rookie Gavin McKenna, the top pick in the draft, scored the go-ahead goal with just over 11 minutes left, and Anthony Stolarz made 20 saves.
buzzRounds.whyCare: The win kept Toronto from its first 10-game losing streak in more than a decade, but the Leafs are still well under .500 at 9-14-3.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: The Leafs finally won on Monday, 4-2 over the Islanders, ending a nine-game losing streak, and the winner came from 18-year-old rookie Gavin McKenna.

details.name: Gavin McKenna
details.buzz: McKenna, the 18-year-old first overall pick, scored the game-winning goal on a rebound with just over 11 minutes left to end Toronto's nine-game skid.

details.name: Anthony Stolarz
details.buzz: Stolarz made 14 of his 20 saves in the first period while the Islanders pushed early, in his fifth start in six games.

buzzRounds.topic: Connor Bedard out four months after shoulder surgery
buzzRounds.whatHappened: The Chicago Blackhawks announced that captain Connor Bedard will miss four months after surgery on his right shoulder. He was hurt taking a faceoff against the Toronto Maple Leafs last week.
buzzRounds.whyCare: Bedard was tied for Chicago's team lead with 18 points in 15 games, and the Blackhawks are already last in the Central Division at 8-14-2.
buzzRounds.youCouldSay: Connor Bedard is out four months after right shoulder surgery, and he was tied for the Blackhawks' lead with 18 points in 15 games.

details.name: Connor Bedard
details.buzz: Bedard, named Chicago's captain in September, had 18 points in 15 games before the right shoulder injury; he also had left shoulder surgery last summer.

details.name: Jake Oettinger
details.buzz: Oettinger has five shutouts, most in the NHL, and 13 wins, tied for second in the league; he is 8-1-1 in his career against Pittsburgh.

hotGoss.topic: Avalanche forward Gabriel Landeskog fined by the NHL
hotGoss.whatHappened: NHL.com reported that the league's Department of Player Safety fined Colorado Avalanche forward Gabriel Landeskog $5,000 for cross-checking (shoving an opponent with the stick held in both hands) Utah forward Logan Cooley in the first period on November 18. Teammate Parker Kelly was fined $3,500 for high-sticking in the same game.
hotGoss.whyTalking: The league fined two Avalanche forwards for separate plays in the same game against the Utah Mammoth.
hotGoss.youCouldSay: The NHL fined Gabriel Landeskog $5,000 for a cross-check on Logan Cooley in the Avalanche game against Utah on November 18.

hotGoss.topic: Kings forward Adrian Kempe fined for high-sticking
hotGoss.whatHappened: NHL.com reported that the league's Department of Player Safety fined Los Angeles Kings forward Adrian Kempe $3,500 for high-sticking (hitting a player with the stick up high) Toronto Maple Leafs forward Dakota Joshua in Toronto on November 19. Kempe was given a double-minor penalty on the play.
hotGoss.whyTalking: The league added a fine the day after the game, on top of the penalty Kempe got during it.
hotGoss.youCouldSay: Adrian Kempe was fined $3,500 by the NHL for a high stick on Dakota Joshua in the Kings game at Toronto on November 19.
